questions.question: If 15th February 2018 was Thursday, then what will be the day on 18th April 2019?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Thursday.**__

 
• The year 2018 is not a **leap year.**
 
• So, 15th February 2019 will be a **Friday.**
 
• The year 2019 is not a leap year so there are **28 days in February.**
 
• So the number of days after 15th February 2019 to 18th April 2019 are **13 + 31 + 18 = 62**
 
• Number of odd days in** 62 days = 6**
 
• Thus, on 18th April 2019, the day will be **Friday + 6 days = Thursday.**
 
• Hence, **"option 4"** is the correct answer.

A father advised his son that the shortest route between Chennai and Mangalore is via Bengaluru.

II. Father gives advice to everyone - **False** (Because the argument only mentions that the father advised *his son*. It does not imply that he gives advice to everyone.)

So, only Assumption I is implicit.

Hence, the correct answer is "**Option 3**".

questions.question: Which types of Hydrogen is produced through the electrolysis of water, leaving nothing but oxygen as a by product?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Green Hydrogen**____.__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**Green Hydrogen:

__
 
• Hydrogen is produced through the electrolysis of water, leaving nothing but oxygen as a byproduct. 
 
• Electrolysis employs an electric current to split water into hydrogen and oxygen in an electrolyzer.
 
• If the electricity is produced by renewable power, such as solar or wind, the resulting pollutant-free hydrogen is called green hydrogen.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

Grey Hydrogen: 

 
• Most hydrogen nowadays comes from natural gas: it is bonded with carbon and can be separated from it via a process involving water called “steam reforming”, but the excess carbon generates CO2.
 
• This hydrogen is called grey whenever the excess CO2 is not captured. 
 
• The majority of chemicals in natural gas contain large amounts of hydrocarbons (hydrogen chemically bonded with carbon).
 
• Catalysts can break these bonds, but the excess carbon then creates CO2 which is not captured and stored.

​Blue Hydrogen:

 
• Blue hydrogen relies on the same process as grey hydrogen, along with carbon capture and storage (CCS).
 
• This eliminates the emissions of grey hydrogen, improving the hydrogen’s environmental impact. 

​Brown Hydrogen: 

 
• Using water and heat, coal can undergo “gasification”.
 
• In this process, the chemicals within coal react to make syngas, which contain a mixture of carbon dioxide (CO2), carbon monoxide (CO), hydrogen, methane and ethylene, along with small quantities of other gases.

questions.question: Which one of the following dynasties ruled as the 'Delhi Sultanate' for a longer period of time ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __Tughluq dynasty__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Tugluq dynasty emerged in 1320 and ended in 1414.
 
• Tughluq dynasty emerged during the period of medieval India and was of Turk-Indian Origin.
 
• The dynasty majorly ruled over the Sultanate of Delhi.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__

Tughluq Dynasty (1320 to 1414):

 
• Ghiyas-ud-din Tughluq or Ghazi Malik was the founder of the Tughluq dynasty.
 
• Ghiyas-ud-din reinstated order in his empire.
 
• He brought Bengal, Utkala or Orissa, and Warangal under his control
 
• The Mongol leaders who invaded North India were seized and confined by him.
 
• In 1325 A.D. Ghiyas-ud-din was crushed to death while attending an event for his victories in Bengal.
 
• Junakhan, the crown prince succeeded him.

Lodi Dynasty (1451 to 1526):

 
• Bahlul Lodi was the founder of the Lodi Dynasty.
 
• Sultanate Period ended with Lodi Dynasty.
 
• He took various measures to gratify his nobles.
 
• Gwalior, Samthal, Sakit, Mewat was conquered by Bahlul Lodi.
 
• He died in 1489 A.D.

Slave Dynasty (1206 to 1290):

 
• The first ruler of the Mamluk Dynasty.
 
• Mamluk Dynasty is also called the Slave Dynasty.
 
• Sold as a slave to Muhammad Ghori, the ruler of Ghor in Afghanistan.
 
• Aibak became Ghori’s trusted general and commander.
 
• He was given charge of Ghori’s Indian possessions after 1192.
 
• When Ghori was assassinated, Aibak declared himself Sultan of Delhi in 1206.
 
• Started construction of the Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque in Delhi. This is one of the first Islamic monuments in northern India.
 
• He began the construction of Qutb Minar in Delhi.
 
• He reigned till his death in 1210. He was said to have been trampled to death by a horse.
 
• He was succeeded by Aram Shah.

 Khilji Dynasty (1290 to 1320):

 
• Jalal-ud-din Firoz Khilji was the founder of the Khilji Dynasty.
 
• He was also called “Clemency Jalal-uddin” as he followed peace and wanted to rule without violence. 
 
• He suppressed Malik Chhajju’s revolt at Kara
 
• He appointed Ala-ud-din Khilji as the Governor of Kara. Alauddin was his son-in-law and also nephew.
 
• In 1292 A.D. Jalal-ud-din defeated the Mongols who had come up to Sunam.
 
• Jalal-ud-din was treacherously murdered by Ala-ud-din Khilji his son-in-law.

questions.question: If an image formed after reflection from a mirror is virtual and highly diminished, then the position of the object and type of mirror is:

options.text: Between C and F and concave mirror
centre of curvature and concave mirror

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**infinity and convex mirror**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **virtual image cannot be obtained on a screen and appears to be formed on the same side of the mirror as the object.**
 
• **A highly diminished image means the image is much smaller in size compared to the object.**
 
• A **convex mirror** always forms a virtual, erect, and diminished image regardless of the position of the object.
 
• A **concave mirror** can form a virtual image, but this happens only when the object is between the focus (F) and the pole (P).
 
• However, the image in this case would be magnified, not diminished.
 
• **For a convex mirror, if the object is at infinity, the image is formed at the focus and is virtual and highly diminished.**
 
• Thus, **a convex mirror with the object at infinity forms a virtual and highly diminished image.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Convex mirror:

 
 
• A spherical mirror whose reflecting surface is curved outwards, is called a convex mirror.
 
• The nature of the image formed by a convex mirror does not depend on the distance of the object from the mirror. 
 
• Convex mirror always forms a virtual, erect and diminished image__ of the object placed at any position in front of the mirror.
 
• Convex mirror is also known as a diverging mirror. 
 
• Convex mirrors are commonly used as rear-view (wing) mirrors in vehicles.
 
• These mirrors are fitted on the sides of the vehicle, enabling the driver to see traffic behind him/her to facilitate safe driving. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e419353f8ea686c4f52bc0ef3be89518be5993f1edd2fccbde193c14d74d401a.png] 

 
• Concave mirror:

 
 
• A spherical mirror, whose reflecting surface is curved inwards, that is, faces towards the center of the sphere, is called a concave mirror.
 
• A concave mirror is also known as a converging mirror.
 
 
• Depending on the point of the object: 
 
• The image may be real or virtual.
 
• image may be erect or inverted.
 
• image may be magnified or diminished.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/081a0abb5ecacee18c46148d9ce7b7507df4621152babf712a9e870dffc51d1f.png] 

 
• Concave mirrors are commonly used in shaving mirrors, torches, search lights and vehicle headlights to get powerful parallel beams of light.

A ray of light is incident on a refracting surface AB of a glass prism and emerges out of the other refracting surface AC. Consider the following statements:

(a) The angle of refraction at surface AB is more than the angle of incidence.

(b) The angle of refraction at the surface AC is less than the angle of incidence.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Neither (a) nor (b).**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The amount of bending depends on the angle at which the light enters the new medium and the refractive index of the medium.
 
• Refracted light bends more in the direction of the normal line when it moves from a less dense material to a denser one.
 
• When a light beam passes from a **rarer medium into a denser medium**, its **angle of refraction is smaller than its angle of incidence.**
 
• When a light beam travels from an optically **denser medium to a rarer medium**, its **angle of refraction is always greater than its angle of incidence.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/dfa94ffab5642c85c209a077da4c3fb9444701f9c396538fa834b360699288d5.png] **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In the field of optics, a prism is a transparent substance, such as glass, that has been precisely cut with plane faces and angles.

 
 
• It is used to reflect and analyze light. 
 
• A standard triangular prism can divide white light into its component colors, or what is known as a spectrum.
 
 
 
• The bending of light as it moves from one transparent substance into another is known as refraction.
 
 
• The bending caused by refraction allows us to create rainbows, prisms, magnifying glasses, and lenses.
 
• Our eyes are dependent on this light bending as well.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements with reference to the Non-Cooperation Movement:

1. Maulana Abul Kalam Azad, M.A. Ansari, Saifuddin Kitchlew and the Ali brothers were the prominent leaders of this movement.

2. August 08, 1920, was fixed as the date of starting the movement.

Which of the above statement is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1 only**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Non-cooperation Movement **

 
 
• **It was Gandhi’s first mass-based political movement.**
 
• This movement was launched as per the resolution taken by the Indian National Congress at the Calcutta session but ratified in the Nagpur session in December 1920.
 
• **August 01, 1920, was fixed as the date of starting the movement. Hence, Statement 2 is not correct.**
 
• **Congress Nagpur session in December 1920 defined the Non - Cooperation program clearly in detail. **
 
• In 1917, Mahatma Gandhi spent most of his time in Champaran fighting for the rights of peasants. He was seeking to obtain the security of tenure as well as freedom in farmers’ choice for the cultivation of crops.
 
• **Then again in 1918, in his home state Gujarat, he was involved in two campaigns. **
 
• The first campaign is about demanding better conditions for textile mill workers.
 
• Then in Kheda, he joined peasants against the state for the remission of taxes at the times of failure of their harvest.
 
• These initiatives taken in the Champaran, Ahmedabad, and Kheda put Gandhi as a nationalist among the people who fought for the poor. But all of these were small localized struggles.
 
• **The main focus of the movement was to boycott schools, colleges, law courts and increase the use of Charkha and using items made in the country.**
 
• **Maulana Abul Kalam Azad, M.A. Ansari, Saifuddin Kitchlew and the Ali brothers were the prominent leaders of the Khilafat Movement, which merged with the Non-Cooperation Movement. Hence, Statement 1 is correct.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **​Khilafat Movement**

 
 
• **The main objective of the Khilafat movement was to force the British government to change its attitude towards Turkey and restore the Khalifa to its former position.**
 
• Turkey was defeated in the First World War and the harsh terms of the Treaty of Sevres (1920) were felt by the Muslims as a great insult to them.
 
• The Muslims in India were upset over the British attitude against Turkey and launched the Khilafat Movement which was jointly led by the Khilafat leaders and the Congress.
 
• In November 1919, a joint conference of the Hindus and the Muslims was held under the chairmanship of Mahatma Gandhi. Mahatma Gandhi was particularly interested in bringing the Hindus and the Muslims together to achieve the country’s independence.
 
• In February 1920, Gandhiji suggested to Khilafat Committee that it adopt a programme of nonviolent non-cooperation to protest the Government’s behaviour.
 
• **On 9 June 1920, the Khilafat Committee at Allahabad unanimously accepted the suggestion of non-cooperation and asked Gandhiji to lead the movement.**
 
• Four stages of non-cooperation were the surrender of titles and honorary positions, resignation from civil services under the Government, resignation from Police and Army services and non-payment of taxes
 
• Subsequently, the Khilafat Movement merged with the Non-Cooperation Movement launched by Mahatma Gandhi in 1920.

questions.question: Who among the following historical musicians is credited with formulating the Sarali Varisa and Sapta Tala Alankaras in the Carnatic Music?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Purandara Dasa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Purandara Dasa** is often referred to as the "Father of Carnatic Music."
 
• He is credited with formulating the **basic lessons** of Carnatic music, known as the **Sarali Varisa** and **Sapta Tala Alankaras**.
 
• These fundamental exercises are essential for beginners to master the swaras (notes) and rhythms of Carnatic music.
 
• Purandara Dasa's compositions are considered foundational for students learning Carnatic music.
 
• He lived in the 16th century and composed thousands of keertanas (devotional songs) in Kannada.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Carnatic Music**

 
 
• It is a classical music form from South India, characterized by a rich and complex system of ragas (melodic frameworks) and talas (rhythmic cycles).
 
• It has a strong emphasis on vocal music, though it is also performed on instruments such as the veena, mridangam, and violin.
 
• Carnatic music is known for its devotional themes, often praising Hindu deities.
 
 
 
• **Sarali Varisa**
 
 
• These are the basic exercises or lessons in Carnatic music that help students practice the swaras (notes) in a simple and systematic manner.
 
• They are designed to familiarize students with the basic patterns and sequences of notes.
 
 
 
• **Sapta Tala Alankaras**
 
 
• These are exercises based on the seven basic talas (rhythmic cycles) in Carnatic music.
 
• Practicing these helps students develop a strong sense of rhythm and timing.
 
 
 
• **Purandara Dasa's Contributions**
 
 
• He composed many kritis (songs) in praise of Lord Vishnu, particularly in his incarnation as Krishna.
 
• His compositions often carry moral and philosophical messages, making them not only musically rich but also spiritually enlightening.

__
 
• **Topic Overview:**

 
 
• The monsoon is a complex meteorological phenomenon involving seasonal changes in atmospheric circulation and precipitation associated with the heating of the land and sea.
 
• The origin and dynamics of the monsoon have been a subject of extensive research, particularly focusing on the impact of the Tibetan Plateau, also known as the "Roof of the World".
 
 
 
• **Koteshwaram and Flohn:**
 
 
• Koteshwaram and Flohn were pioneering meteorologists who established the thermal impact of the Tibetan Plateau on the origin of the monsoon.
 
• They posited that the elevated landmass of the Tibetan Plateau significantly influences the atmospheric circulation by heating the air above it during summer.
 
• This heating results in a pressure gradient that draws moist air from the Indian Ocean, leading to the characteristic heavy rains of the monsoon season.
 
• Their work has been fundamental in understanding the monsoon dynamics and has provided critical insights into weather prediction models.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• Anant Krishna is not known for establishing the thermal impact of the Tibetan Plateau on the monsoon.
 
• While he may have contributed to meteorological studies, his work does not directly relate to the key findings of Koteshwaram and Flohn.
 
 
 
• **T. M. Yin:**
 
 
• T. M. Yin's contributions to meteorology are significant but not specifically related to the thermal impact of the Tibetan Plateau on the monsoon.
 
• His research may focus on other aspects of atmospheric sciences or different regions.
 
 
 
• **Raman and Ramanathan:**
 
 
• Raman and Ramanathan have made notable contributions to the field of meteorology and atmospheric sciences.
 
• However, their work did not specifically establish the thermal impact of the Tibetan Plateau on the monsoon, which is the key discovery attributed to Koteshwaram and Flohn.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

questions.question: When the length of the shadow of a building is equal to the height of the building, Find the elevation of source of light.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When the **Height** of an object is equal to the length of its **Shadow**, the triangle formed is an **Isosceles Right-Angled Triangle**.

In such cases, the ratio of **Height : Shadow** is 1 : 1.

Since tan θ = 1, the **Angle of Elevation** is always **45°**.

**∴ The correct answer is 45°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Let the **Height of the building** be AB = h.

Let the **Length of the shadow** be BC = s.

Let the **Angle of elevation** of the source of light be θ.

⇒ Given: **Height = Shadow** ⇒ h = s

⇒ In right-angled ΔABC, tan θ = **Perpendicular** ÷ **Base**

⇒ tan θ = AB ÷ BC

⇒ tan θ = h ÷ s

⇒ tan θ = h ÷ h (Substitute s = h)

⇒ tan θ = 1

⇒ tan θ = tan 45°

⇒ θ = 45°

**∴ The correct answer is 45°.**

Standard Trigonometric Ratios

Angle of Elevation and Depression

The **Angle of Elevation** is measured upward from the horizontal, while the **Angle of Depression** is measured downward from the horizontal.

Isosceles Right Triangle Property

In a right-angled triangle, if the two legs are equal, the remaining two angles must both be 45°.</p

questions.question: A rides his bicycle at 15 km/h, while B starts his ride after 6 hours to catch A with a speed of 25 km/h. Time taken by B to catch A (in hours) is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Lead distance created by **A** = 15 × 6 = 90 km.

Relative speed (same direction) = 25 − 15 = 10 km/h.

Time taken by **B** to catch **A** = Lead Distance ÷ Relative Speed = 90 ÷ 10 = 9 hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 9 hr.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of **A** = 15 km/h

Speed of **B** = 25 km/h

Time gap = 6 hours

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b10ee40206aa5707bf5b081aec046c03eb08e156c4f7477a99189f6968a0ee55.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

**Calculations:**

⇒ Distance covered by **A** in 6 hours = 15 × 6 = 90 km

⇒ When **B** starts, the distance between **A** and **B** is 90 km.

⇒ Relative speed of **B** relative to **A** = 25 − 15 = 10 km/h

⇒ Time taken by **B** to cover the gap = 90 ÷ 10

⇒ Time taken = 9 hr

**∴ The correct answer is 9 hr.**

**__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed (Same Direction)

When two objects move in the same direction, the relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds (S₁ − S₂).

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction)

When two objects move toward each other, the relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂).

Meeting Time Rule

The time required for a faster object to catch a slower object is given by: Meeting Time = (Initial separation distance) ÷ (Relative Speed).</p

Difference in effective rate = 19.1016% − 18.72% = 0.3816%

Difference in amount = 0.3816% of 2,50,000 = (0.3816 ÷ 100) × 250000 = ₹954

**∴ The correct answer is ₹954.**

Principal (P) = ₹2,50,000

⇒ A₁ = 250000 × (1 + 12/100) × (1 + 6/100)

⇒ A₁ = 250000 × 1.12 × 1.06 = 250000 × 1.1872

⇒ A₁ = ₹2,96,800

⇒ Amount compounded semi-annually (A₂) = P × (1 + (R/2)/100)²T

⇒ A₂ = 250000 × (1 + 6/100)³

⇒ A₂ = 250000 × (1.06)³ = 250000 × 1.191016

⇒ A₂ = ₹2,97,754

⇒ Difference in amounts = A₂ − A₁

⇒ Difference = 297754 − 296800 = ₹954

**∴ The correct answer is ₹954.**

Select the correct active form of the given sentence.

Two more steel plants will be set up by Mittal and Co.

options.text: Mittal and Co. will be setting up two more steel plants.

Mittal and Co. will set up two more steel plants.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Mittal and Co. will set up two more steel plants.**'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in passive voice and the tense is future indefinite which is used to indicate an action or occurrence that has not happened yet and will take place at some point in the future.
 
• The structure in active and passive voice for the future indefinite tense is as following:
 
 
• Active structure__: Sub (performer of the action) + will/shall + object (receiver of the action)
 
• __Passive structure:__ Sub (receiver of the action) + will be + V3 + by + object (performer of the action).
 
 
 
• ​To change the given sentence into active voice,
 __
 
• **Start **the sentence with the **performer **of the action 'Mittal and Co.'
 
• After that '**will + set up (V1)__**' takes place.
 
• The **receiver of the action** of the verb '__**two more steel plants**__' will be placed.
 
 
 
• On following the above steps, we get the required active form of the sentence:
 __
 
• ***Mittal and Co. will set up two more steel plants***.
 
 

*Therefore, the **correct **answer is option **3**)*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• When the subject of a sentence** performs the verb’s action**, we say that the sentence is in the** active voice**.
 
• When the subject is acted on by the verb (in other words; **receives the action of the verb**), the sentence is in p**assive voice**.

questions.question: In the context of the passage, which of the following is the closest antonym to the word "reticence" as used in the second paragraph ("forces victims into a coerced reticence")?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 3) i.e. Candor**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

The word **"reticence"**, as used in the passage, refers to the quality of being reserved or restrained in speech; reluctance to speak or express one's thoughts. (मौनव्रत, चुप्पी)

Let's analyze each option to find the closest antonym:

 
• **Trepidation:** Means a feeling of fear or anxiety about something that may happen. (भय, घबराहट)

 
 
• This word does not convey the opposite of "reticence" and is not related to the willingness to speak or express oneself.
 
 
 
• **Acquiescence:** Means the reluctant acceptance of something without protest. (अनुकूलता, सहमति)
 
 
• This word suggests passive acceptance rather than the active communication of one's thoughts, making it less appropriate as an antonym to "reticence."
 
 
 
• **Candor:** Means the quality of being open and honest in expression; frankness. (खुलापन, स्पष्टवादिता)
 
 
• This word is opposite in meaning to "reticence," as it denotes being open and willing to communicate rather than being reserved or silent.
 
 
 
• **Stoicism:** Means the endurance of pain or hardship without the display of feelings and without complaint. (धैर्य, मानसिक संतुलन)
 
 
• This word refers to emotional resilience and is not directly related to the willingness to speak or express oneself, making it less appropriate as an antonym to "reticence."

questions.question: It can be reasonably inferred from the passage that the author's use of the phrase "sanctity of the familial unit" most likely suggests that:
